name: Bishr ibn Muhammad al-Sakhtiyani

taqrib.en: Truthful; accused of holding the Murji'a view on faith.

role: Teacher of al-Bukhari; used by none of the other five compilers

verdicts.ar: ذكره في الثقات وقال: كان مرجئا
verdicts.en: Listed him in al-Thiqat and said: he was a Murji'.

flags.label: Accused of irja'
flags.detail: The only note against him is theological, not a question of memory or honesty: Ibn Hibban says he held the Murji'a position that deeds are not part of faith. The critics did not treat it as affecting his transmission, and al-Bukhari used him in the Sahih, though only al-Bukhari of the six did.

flags.label: Thin biography
flags.detail: The rijal works preserve little about him beyond his name, trade, teachers and death date. Ibn Hajar notes that Ibn Abi Hatim lists a Bishr ibn Muhammad separately from al-Sakhtiyani and that the two may be one person.

bio: A leather-dealer of Marw who studied with Ibn al-Mubarak and whom al-Bukhari heard, probably in Khurasan. He appears in the Sahih as the second of al-Bukhari's two teachers for this hadith, carrying the version in which Ibn al-Mubarak joins Yunus and Ma'mar. His kunya Abu Muhammad matches his father's name.

provenance.ref: Shamela narrator record 941, drawing on Tahdhib al-Kamal 4/145 and Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 1/231
